rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is exactly the kind of help that matters right now, and there's a concrete, data-analyst-shaped task waiting. Quick honesty note first: this reply is drafted and sent by the AI assistant Morgan uses to run Halcyon Threshold's operations. Morgan reads everything and will follow up personally. The task: a \"gap map\" of what independent groups already measure in AI safety. Halcyon Threshold's core idea is to measure something nobody is currently measuring — evals, trackers, audits — and publish it openly. But \"nobody\" is a claim that needs checking. So before picking a target, we want a structured inventory of what exists: eval suites, incident databases, trackers of lab safety commitments, governance/policy trackers, and so on — who runs each, what exactly it measures, how often, whether it's still maintained, and whether the data is open. What it would look like: - A spreadsheet, one row per project. Suggested columns: name, url, org_or_person, what_measured (one specific sentence), object_type (model-behaviour / lab-commitments / incidents / policy / compute / public-opinion / other), method, cadence, last_updated, data_open (yes/partial/no), maintained (yes/stale/dead), notes. - Breadth first — maybe 60–100 rows — then a closer look at three areas we're especially curious about: (1) promised-vs-done tracking of labs' published safety commitments, (2) longitudinal tracking of safety behaviour across successive versions of the same model family, (3) audits of how complete and timely public AI-incident databases are. - At the end, a page or two: what's well covered, what's thin, what's absent. Rough timeline: a first pass by around 5 December if that fits your five hours a week — but please tell us what's realistic rather than the other way round. Share it however is easiest (a Google Sheet link or a CSV by email is perfect). If you'd like, send a first ten rows after week one so we can check the schema is working before you go wide. If this isn't the kind of thing you had in mind, say so — there'll be other work soon, particularly once we start the actual measurement in December. Thanks again, Priya. — Halcyon Threshold operations (AI assistant), on behalf of Morgan Hale"
rows.quote: Priya Raman** — replied (private, signed as your AI assistant) with a concrete 5h/week task: the gap-map inventory
